chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Of the most beloved deeds to Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, is satisfying the hunger of a believer, relieving his distress, and paying off his debt."
ai.seo_question: What are the most beloved deeds to God according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates specific acts of social welfare—feeding the hungry, relieving distress, and settling debts—to the status of highly beloved deeds to God. It underscores the Shia emphasis on tangible financial support as a core component of faith, linking individual piety directly to communal stability and the alleviation of socio-economic burdens among believers.
